Abstract
Cloud computing systems provide highly available and scalable computing, storage, and network resources to 
meet various service demands. Anomaly detection based on monitoring metrics plays a crucial role in identifying 
system defects and abnormal behaviors, ensuring the reliability and stability of cloud services. However, as the 
complexity of data increases and concurrent noise impacts cloud environments, server failures and abnormal 
events rise, making anomaly detection more challenging. To address these issues, we propose MemGT, an 
unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly detection method that offers high accuracy, good robustness, and 
noise resistance for various data patterns in complex cloud environments. Our approach utilizes a Transformer 
encoder and dynamic graph structure learning to extract spatio-temporal features of monitoring metrics in cloud 
computing systems in parallel. Additionally, we introduce a novel dynamic gated memory module to guide the 
Transformer encoder in extracting hidden features, thereby enhancing the model’s robustness to varying data 
patterns in dynamic cloud environments. To accurately distinguish between concurrent noise and real anomalies, 
we utilize a window-wise graph learning method, further improving the model’s noise resistance. We compared 
the detection performance of MemGT with 15 baseline methods across 8 public datasets. The experimental 
results demonstrate that our method achieves an average F1 score of 95.04%, surpassing state-of-the-art baseline 
methods by 24.80%.

Introduction
Cloud computing systems consist of a large number of 
servers, networks, and storage devices that work together 
to provide highly available and scalable computing and 
storage services [1]. Accurate detection of performance 
anomalies, such as high CPU utilization or unexpected 
workload spikes, can help operators ensure system con­
tinuity and maintain service reliability [2, 3]. However, 
the complex architecture and network topology of cloud 
infrastructures increase the risk of cascading failures and 
security vulnerabilities [4]. In addition, the growing inter­
action between services and workloads changing in cloud 
applications increases the complexity of cloud comput­
ing systems [5, 6]. As a result, anomaly detection in cloud 
computing systems has become increasingly challenging, 
driving the demand for robust detection methods with 
higher accuracy and lower false alarm rates.
In cloud computing systems, monitoring metrics col­
lected from server nodes are often represented as mul­
tivariate time series data, which can be analyzed for 
anomaly detection to deliver fault warnings and maintain 
system stability [7]. For example, during traffic surges, 
metrics such as network bandwidth, CPU utilization, 
and memory usage can help identify performance bottle­
necks or resource contention issues. Various methods 
have been proposed for multivariate time series anomaly 
detection in cloud computing systems [8]. Traditional 
machine learning approaches, based on statistical or 
classification principles, are effective for simple tasks 
but struggle with the complex nonlinear relationships in 
cloud environments [9]. Recently, deep learning models, 
such as recurrent neural networks (RNN) and long short-
term memory (LSTM) networks, have shown promise in 
capturing short-term dependencies and addressing local 
intricacies [10, 11]. Unlike RNNs and LSTMs, the Trans­
former model, leveraging a self-attention mechanism, 
efficiently captures dependencies and models contextual 
information across multivariate time series, enabling 
precise anomaly detection in extended sequences [12]. 
However, these models still struggle to address challenges 
such as high dimensionality, concurrency, and noise of 
monitoring metrics in cloud computing systems.
Anomaly detection based on monitoring metrics in 
cloud environments remains a significant challenge. 
First, the growing number of monitoring metrics in cloud 
infrastructures increases data dimensionality, while exist­
ing unsupervised methods primarily focus on temporal 
patterns, often overlooking inter-dimensional correla­
tions. Second, the highly dynamic nature of cloud envi­
ronments introduces diverse data patterns, yet most 
detection methods are designed for specific scenarios, 
resulting in limited accuracy and real-time performance 
[13, 14]. Moreover, servers and components in cloud 
systems generate data concurrently, leading to concur­
rent noise that significantly impacts detection accuracy 
[15, 16]. Concurrent noise arises from the simultaneous 
execution of multiple tasks, processes, or data streams in 
the cloud environment. During periods of unstable net­
work traffic or high system load, multiple dimensions of 
performance data may be influenced by concurrent noise 
[15]. As shown in Fig. 1, concurrent noise results in erro­
neous observations rather than actual anomalies, leading 
to an increase of the false positive rate in anomaly detec­
tion tasks.
To address the above challenges, this paper aims to 
design a robust and accurate unsupervised anomaly

detection model for highly dynamic cloud computing

following three research questions:
RQ1: How to accurately extract complex spatio-
temporal dependencies from monitoring metrics in 
cloud environments while meeting the requirements 
of real-time anomaly detection?
RQ2: How to improve the robustness of anomaly 
detection models to handle diverse data patterns 
and adapt to dynamic conditions in complex cloud 
environments?
RQ3: How to accurately model concurrent noise 
in cloud environments and enhance the model’s 
resistance to noise?
To answer these questions, we propose MemGT, an 
unsupervised anomaly detection method that leverages 
both a Transformer encoder and dynamic graph struc­
ture learning in parallel to extract robust spatio-tem­
poral features from monitoring metrics. By interacting 
with a dynamic gated memory module, MemGT adapts 
to changes in data patterns, enabling precise extraction 
of complex features and improving its robustness. Given 
that concurrent noise stems from disrupted observations 
rather than actual anomalies, we utilize a novel window-
wise Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to model the 
concurrent noise, thereby enhancing the model’s noise 
resistance.
The two-stage training framework is adopted for 
MemGT to addresses two key challenges in highly 
dynamic cloud environments. Firstly, in unsupervised 
scenarios, randomly initialized memory units may 
struggle to capture diverse normal patterns within data, 
particularly in high-dimensional, noisy cloud environ­
ments. Secondly, monitoring metric patterns in cloud 
environments can dynamically evolve over time, ren­
dering a single static memory insufficient to cover all 
normal patterns. Thus, in the first stage, we leverage 
K-means clustering on the query vectors extracted by 
the Transformer encoder to initialize memory units with 
representative normal patterns, avoiding the instability 
and pattern redundancy caused by random initializa­
tion. Subsequently, in the second stage, these initialized 
memory units guide the reconstruction process through 
an iterative update mechanism where both memory units 
and query vectors are dynamically adjusted via the gated 
mechanism. The initialized memory units serve as stable 
anchors for anomaly discrimination, while their dynamic 
updating through training helps adapt to evolving data 
patterns in cloud environments.
The contributions of this paper are as follows:
 	•
We utilize a Transformer encoder and a dynamic 
graph structure learning approach to extract 
spatio-temporal features from monitoring metrics, 
effectively addressing the issues of high-dimensional 
dependency.
 	•
We design a novel dynamic gated memory module 
that can introduce new prototype features based 
on training conditions and iteratively update them, 
thereby improving the robustness of the model.
 	•
We employ a window-wise GCN to model 
concurrent noise in data, which significantly 
enhances the noise resistance ability of the model.
 	•
We provide empirical evaluation for MemGT on 
eight real-world public datasets, and results show 
that MemGT achieves state-of-the-art performance 
compared with other benchmark detection methods.

Related work
In this section, we first introduce deep learning-based 
unsupervised anomaly detection methods, including 
graph structure learning-based and transformer-based 
methods. Then, we provide a detailed introduction to the 
memory network-based anomaly detection methods.
Deep learning-based unsupervised anomaly detection
Deep Learning-based unsupervised deep learning meth­
ods have become the mainstream direction of anomaly 
detection due to their low cost and high adaptability 
[17]. DAGMM [18] combines Deep Autoencoder (DAE) 
with Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) by compressing 
time series into a latent space and modeling the prob­
ability density within this latent space to identify anoma­
lies. OmniAnomaly [11] employs a stochastic RNN to 
capture the complexity and uncertainty in time series 
and then utilizes a planar normalization flow to com­
pute reconstruction probabilities for anomaly detection. 
LSTM-VAE [19] employs LSTM as the fundamental 
framework to learn temporal patterns within time series 
data and utilizes Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) to cap­
ture efficient data representations. USAD [20] utilizes 
an encoder-decoder architecture for adversarial train­
ing, enabling it to learn how to amplify anomaly recon­
struction errors, which improves stability compared to 
methods based on Generative Adversarial Networks 
(GAN). MTAD-GAT [21] incorporates parallel feature-
directed and time-directed graph attention layers that

adopts a max-min strategy and calculates the association 
weight distribution of each time point with the entire 
sequence to capture complex dynamic dependencies 
within the time series.
In summary, while these methods utilize deep learning 
models to achieve unsupervised anomaly detection, the 
complexity and dynamic nature of data in cloud com­
puting systems often limit their detection accuracy and 
robustness.
Memory network-based detection methods
Early memory networks predominantly utilized external 
memory matrices as the primary mechanism to enhance 
the memory capabilities of neural networks. [26]. 
Recently, memory networks have been widely applied in 
the field of anomaly detection. MemAE [27] is the first 
unsupervised anomaly detection model that combines 
memory networks with autoencoders and is capable of 
utilizing normal samples’ information to identify anoma­
lies. However, its memory network cannot be updated in 
real-time during the training process. MNAD [28] pro­
poses a new memory update strategy, which updates the 
memory network only when normal samples are encoun­
tered, preventing it from learning anomaly sample fea­
tures. However, this method only injects the weighted 
sum of queries into the memory network without con­
sidering the degree of the update. Building upon the pre­
vious work, MEMTO [29] introduces a gated memory 
module, which is capable of adapting to various normal 
patterns in a data-driven manner. It has achieved excel­
lent results in addressing over-generalization issues and 
enhancing anomaly detection accuracy.
In summary, the highly dynamic, high-dimensional, 
and noisy monitoring metrics in cloud environments can 
limit the accuracy of existing anomaly detection meth­
ods. To address these challenges, we introduce a dynamic 
gated memory module integrated with a Transformer 
encoder in MemGT to enhance model robustness.

Concurrent noise recognition
Concurrent noise tends to cause large errors simultane­
ously among multiple features of the input sub-series 
within a certain time frame [16]. To minimize the impact 
of concurrent noise on anomaly detection, MemGT 
applies spatial correlation modeling to the reconstructed 
monitoring metrics, enabling the filtering out of con­
current noise from identified potential anomalies. Cur­
rent static GNN approaches can only capture global and 
stable dependencies between variables, and dynamic 
GNN methods only predict the evolving dynamic depen­
dencies between variables along the timestamp, making 
neither suitable for modeling random concurrent noise.

autoencoder architecture with an adversarial 
training framework, achieving anomaly detection by 
amplifying the reconstruction error of anomalies.

Parameter settings
We implement our approach using the PyTorch frame­
work on an NVIDIA GTX 4060 Ti 16GB GPU. We gen­
erate sub-series by applying a non-overlapped sliding 
window with a length of 100 to obtain fixed-length inputs 
for each dataset, and set the batch size for each time step 
to 256, the number of iterations to 100, and implement 
an early stop mechanism with the patience of 10. Our 
model employs the Adam optimizer, with a learning rate 
of 5e−4 for the first phase of training and 1e−4 for the 
second phase. We set the initial number of memory units 
M to 10, the maximum number of newly added memory 
units AN to 3, and the coefficient of entropy loss α, the 
coefficient of concurrent noise loss β, and the tempera­
ture parameter τ in the softmax function to 0.001, 0.01, 
and 0.05, respectively.

Performance analysis
The superior performance of MemGT across diverse 
datasets can be attributed to its unique architectural 
components effectively addressing the core challenges in 
cloud anomaly detection. We provide a detailed analy­
sis comparing MemGT with key baselines based on the 
results in Table 3:
1) Compared to Graph-based Methods (GDN, MTAD-
GAT): MemGT consistently outperforms these 
methods, particularly on complex datasets. On 
WADI (127 dimension), MemGT achieves an F1 
of 0.8545, surpassing GDN by +42.85% (0.8545 
vs 0.4260) and MTAD-GAT by +43.76% (0.8545 
vs 0.4169). This substantial improvement is due 
to MemGT’s Dynamic Graph Structure Learning 
(DGTL) module, which learns adjacency matrices 
per sub-series, adapting to the highly dynamic 
correlations in cloud metrics, unlike static or globally 
learned graphs in GDN/MTAD-GAT. Improvement 
are also clear on AstrosetLow (MemGT 0.9781 vs 
GDN 0.4545: +52.36%).
2) Compared to Transformer-based Methods 
(TranAD, Anomaly Transformer): MemGT shows 
strong improvements over TranAD and Anomaly 
Transformer where long-term patterns and noise 
robustness are critical. On WADI, MemGT (0.8545) 
leads TranAD (0.5391) by +31.54% and Anomaly 
Transformer (0.7044) by +15.01%. On the noisy 
AstrosetLow, MemGT (0.9781) outperforms 
TranAD (0.4728) by +50.53%. This is attributed 
to MemGT’s Dynamic Gated Memory Module 
(DGMM), which stores/updates normal prototypes, 
improves reconstruction fidelity for normal points 
under diverse patterns, and its dedicated Concurrent 
Noise Recognition (CNR) module. Note: On PSM, 
MemGT (0.9790) shows a marginal improvement 
over Anomaly Transformer (0.9751, +0.39%) and 
TranAD (0.8782, +10.08%), consistent with its design 
but less dramatic than on noisy datasets.
3) Compared to Memory-based Methods (MEMTO): 
MemGT generally matches or exceeds MEMTO, 
with crucial gains in noisy/high-dim scenarios. 
On WADI, MemGT (0.8545) leads MEMTO 
(0.4397) by +41.48%. On AstrosetLow, MemGT 
(0.9781) surpasses MEMTO (0.9571) by +2.1%. 
The key differentiator is MemGT’s CNR module 
explicitly modeling and filtering concurrent noise 
via window-wise GCN, which MEMTO lacks. Note: 
On AstrosetHigh, MEMTO (0.9595) achieves a very 
slight edge over MemGT (0.9605, −0.10% difference). 
This minor variance is likely within the margin of 
experimental stochasticity for this specific dataset, 
and MemGT maintains superior performance on the 
more challenging AstrosetLow.
4) Compared to Recent SOTA (DCdetector, STEN, 
GDformer): MemGT demonstrates clear advantages 
where dynamic dependencies and noise are 
prevalent. On WADI, MemGT (0.8545) outperforms 
DCdetector (0.6654, +18.91%), STEN (0.7843, 
+7.02%), and GDformer (0.7159, +13.86%). On 
AstrosetLow, MemGT (0.9781) leads DCdetector 
(0.5841, +39.40%), STEN (0.9468, +3.13%), and 
GDformer (0.7719, +20.62%). MemGT’s integrated 
DGSL (dynamic graphs) and CNR (noise filtering) 
provide this edge over methods relying solely on 
contrastive learning (DCdetector), static spatio-
temporal norms (STEN), or global dictionaries 
(GDformer). Note: On SWaT, DCdetector achieves 
a higher F1 (0.9615) than MemGT (0.9500, −1.15% 
difference). This suggests DCdetector’s contrastive

strength in noise resistance (CNR) may be less 
critical here. However, MemGT maintains superior 
robustness across the broader range of datasets, 
especially the noisier ones.

Real-time performance analysis
In this study, we evaluate the real-time performance of 
MemGT, including training costs and inference speed.
Training costs
In Table 5, we detail the training costs of MemGT on five 
large-scale datasets, using training time (seconds), Ran­
dom Access Memory (RAM) consumption (MB), and 
Video Random Access Memory (VRAM) consumption 
(MB) as metrics. The results, compared to three deep 
learning baselines, demonstrate that MemGT exhib­
its a significant advantage in training speed. It achieves 
the lowest training time on four out of the five datas­
ets. For example, on the WADI dataset, its training time 
(59 seconds) is only 12.5% of that required by Anomaly 
Transformer (471 seconds). Similarly, on the SMAP data­
set, it takes only 52 seconds, which is approximately 20 
times faster than DCdetector (1038 seconds). However, 
MemGT’s resource consumption is generally higher than 
other methods. Notably, on the PSM and SWaT datas­
ets, MemGT’s VRAM usage is several times higher than 
that of the most efficient method, GDformer. Neverthe­
less, this represents a reasonable trade-off resulting from 
increased model complexity. From a real-time processing 
perspective, MemGT maintains optimal performance for 
time-sensitive tasks.
Inference speed
Anomaly detection systems deployed in cloud environ­
ments typically require swift identification of anomalies 
and timely responses. Otherwise, cascading anomalies 
may occur and rapidly spread, causing more severe dam­
age. Therefore, we record the inference speed of MemGT 
across eight datasets. The experimental results in Table 
6 show that the inference speed of MemGT on a single 
sample is at the microsecond level, which can meet the 
real-time detection of anomalies in cloud computing sys­
tems. Furthermore, this level of efficiency is critical for 
real-time monitoring and rapid response in resource-
constrained IoT edge environments. In general, MemGT 
demonstrates excellent performance in handling various 
anomaly detection tasks in highly dynamic cloud envi­
ronments and shows promising applicability to IoT sce­
narios demanding high accuracy, noise resilience, and 
real-time processing.

Conclusion and future work
In cloud computing systems, anomaly detection for 
performance degradation faces challenges of highly 
dynamic, high-dimensional, and noisy monitoring met­
rics. To address these issues, this paper presents MemGT, 
an unsupervised anomaly detection approach that com­
bines a memory-augmented Transformer with dynamic 
graph structure learning. MemGT effectively captures 
intricate spatio-temporal dependencies in input data and 
effectively tackles the problem of reduced anomaly detec­
tion accuracy with high-dimensional datasets. Experi­
ment results indicate that MemGT outperforms other 
state-of-the-art baselines. Additionally, the window-wise 
graph learning technique we employ is capable of captur­
ing concurrent noise within the dataset, further enhanc­
ing the model’s noise resistance.
While the MemGT framework is primarily designed 
and optimized for detecting performance anomalies in 
highly dynamic cloud environments, our experimental 
results on diverse datasets reveal its broader potential. 
However, it is important to note that while the funda­
mental techniques show promise, optimal application 
in non-cloud domains might require domain-specific 
adaptations. For instance, the physical interpreta­
tion and patterns of ‘concurrent noise’ may differ (e.g., 
cloud occlusion in astronomy vs. resource contention in 
clouds), potentially necessitating adjustments to the CNR 
module’s design or input features.
In the future, we will explore explicitly tailoring and 
evaluating MemGT for specific non-cloud applications, 
investigated necessary adaptations, and further enhanc­
ing its capabilities as a general-purpose robust anomaly 
detection framework for complex, dynamic, and noisy 
multivariate time series data.

Abstract: Cloud computing systems provide highly available and scalable computing, storage, and network resources to meet various service demands. Anomaly detection based on monitoring metrics plays a crucial role in identifying system defects and abnormal behaviors, ensuring the reliability and stability of cloud services. However, as the complexity of data increases and concurrent noise impacts cloud environments, server failures and abnormal events rise, making anomaly detection more challenging. To address these issues, we propose MemGT, an unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly detection method that offers high accuracy, good robustness, and noise resistance for various data patterns in complex cloud environments. Our approach utilizes a Transformer encoder and dynamic graph structure learning to extract spatio-temporal features of monitoring metrics in cloud computing systems in parallel. Additionally, we introduce a novel dynamic gated memory module to guide the Transformer encoder in extracting hidden features, thereby enhancing the model’s robustness to varying data patterns in dynamic cloud environments. To accurately distinguish between concurrent noise and real anomalies, we utilize a window-wise graph learning method, further improving the model’s noise resistance. We compared the detection performance of MemGT with 15 baseline methods across 8 public datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves an average F1 score of 95.04%, surpassing state-of-the-art baseline methods by 24.80%.
